items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: Lou was responsible for me playing trombone.

ctx.x: Well you know we kind of skipped over some early influences. You mentioned that your father was a musician and had a family orientation there with the music. The trombone players — I think I read that Cutty Cutshall and Lou McGarity were people that you aspired to.

Lou was responsible for me playing trombone. I just heard his recording of “Yours” with the Benny Goodman Orchestra, I think it was 1941 or ‘42. He played an eight bar solo there, and I heard it and I said that’s what I want to play.
Eight bars and you knew what you wanted to do. That’s saying something.
